sections.overview: This small poison frog is native to northern Peru, where its warning colours vary geographically.
sections.identification: Several local colour forms resemble those of other poisonous Ranitomeya frogs, a pattern associated with Müllerian mimicry.
sections.habitat: It occurs in the Peruvian departments of San Martín and Loreto, in forest where it uses small water-filled plant cavities for its larvae.
sections.diet: The consulted field study focuses on reproduction and does not establish a species-specific wild diet.
sections.behavior: The species shares locally similar warning patterns with other defended frogs, though its pattern forms also differ across its range.
sections.reproduction: Eggs are laid in water held by Heliconia or Xanthosoma; both parents care for the young, and females feed tadpoles with unfertilized eggs.
sections.ecology: Its mimicry system has made this species a subject of research on warning signals and reproductive isolation.
sections.conservation: The sources used here document its biology but do not provide a current global conservation assessment.
